design_date_source: cycle 004 first trial start (brief table); Exscientia F-1 filed 2021-09-10 gives December 16, 2020: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1865408/000110465921114491/tm2119783-5_f1.htm
method_quote: The A2a receptor antagonist, which is in development for adult patients with advanced solid tumours, was co-invented and developed between Exscientia and Evotec, including application of Exscientia’s next generation 3-D evolutionary AI-design platform, Centaur Chemist ® .
note: Release does not use the code name; it names the A2a antagonist that entered trials, which the F-1 identifies as EXS21546. 'Evolutionary AI-design' coded G3 (an algorithm proposes molecules; Exscientia's F-1 calls its evolutionary design algorithm Gambit 'a generative molecule design algorithm'). The F-1 (2021-09-10) also says Exscientia's deep-learning image platform was used to assess EXS21546 in patient tissue (G1), but that is testing after design, not design. Design date: F-1 says the trial started December 16, 2020, not 2020-12-08; no company-stated nomination date found (F-1 says the candidate was found nine months after project start, undated).

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (same release announces Phase 1 already initiated)
method_quote: Novel compounds are automatically designed and prioritised for synthesis by its AI systems, which rapidly evolve compounds towards the desired candidate criteria for clinical development.
later_quote: We use AI methods, including evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement learning, deep learning and active learning, to design virtually all of our novel molecules.
note: Candidate-level sentence in the same release names only the platform: 'Exscientia applying its Centaur ChemistTM Artificial Intelligence (AI) platform for drug discovery'. Method taken from the Exscientia platform paragraph of the same joint release (platform level). 'automatically designed ... evolve compounds' coded G3 and 'prioritised for synthesis' coded G1; this is a functional description, not a named algorithm. Later attribution is platform-level (F-1), not candidate-specific; F-1 does not name DSP-1181. First trial start date within January 2020 not stated.

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (already listed at Phase 1 in the U.S.)
method_quote: Novel compounds are automatically designed and prioritised for synthesis by its AI systems, which rapidly evolve compounds towards the desired candidate criteria for clinical development.
later_quote: Using the first generation of our design platform we also developed additional drug candidates through a pilot "design as a service" (DaaS) programme with Sumitomo Pharma, including DSP-0038, currently in Phase 1 studies.
note: No candidate-level method found. Sumitomo says only 'discovered at Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma using Exscientia's AI technologies' (ebr20210512.2). The F-1 (2021-09-10, within window) says 'Our AI platform has designed bispecific compounds that simultaneously fulfil the binding site requirements of two targets through an integrated pharmacophore' and 'We designed small molecule DSP-0038'; an integrated pharmacophore is not an ML method, so not used. Platform source: the Exscientia platform paragraph in the January 2020 joint release, the last Exscientia platform description found that certainly precedes the trial (exact first trial start unknown, on or before 2021-05-12). The Evotec release of 2021-04-09 ('3-D evolutionary AI-design platform') is closer in date and gives the same vintage, but may post-date the trial start. Not on ClinicalTrials.gov.

method_quote: We use AI methods, including evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement learning, deep learning and active learning, to design virtually all of our novel molecules.

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (EXS617, F-1); development candidate nomination announced 2021-11-17 without a date
method_quote: By leveraging AI models and active learning, Exscientia was able to design an orally bioavailable, highly potent and selective small-molecule antagonist of CDK7, GTAEXS-617, currently in IND-enabling studies as a potential treatment for transcriptionally addicted cancers, including ovarian and breast cancer.
later_quote: Designed entirely using our AI-led platform, REC-617 was synthesized from hit to candidate in just under 12 months, requiring only 136 novel molecules—an order of magnitude more efficient than conventional drug discovery.
note: 'AI models' unspecified; active learning is G1. Exscientia 20-F filed 2024-03-21 (within window, trial start 2023-07-06) gives the same: CDK7 'Key Exscientia Tech' cell reads 'Active learning and machine learning to design optimal in vivo PK/PD parameters and human dose' (G1). The 6-K exhibit is a Business Wire release filed on EDGAR.

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (Recursion 10-Q for Q2 2021)
method_quote: REC-3964 is a new chemical entity that was identified with our brute-force approach which utilized phenomics to identify cellular and structural changes in epithelial cells associated with the pathological changes resulting from exposure to C. difficile toxins. Structure-activity-relationship (SAR) was driven through the Recursion OS to identify structural series that restored structural defects resulting from C. difficile toxins’ effects.
later_quote: Identified using Recursion’s AI-driven phenotypic screening platform, REC-3964 demonstrated potent toxin inhibition and barrier restoration in preclinical studies.
note: Candidate sentence names phenomics (image-based screening) and the Recursion OS; the same 10-K describes the platform as 'the transformation of our images into mathematical representations through our in-house proprietary convolutional neural networks' (machine learning on cell images, G1). Earlier 10-K filed 2022-03-23 says only 'We identified early molecules in the series on the Recursion OS using gut epithelial cells exposed to C. difficile Toxin B.' Phase 1 start in 2022 per this 10-K; no ClinicalTrials.gov record of that Phase 1 found (NCT06536465 is a later Phase 2, start 2024-10-14).

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (Schrödinger 10-Q for Q1 2022)
method_quote: Combining multi-parameter optimization, FEP+, and machine learning, we were able to prioritize tight-binding compounds with drug-like properties, and identified multiple novel and distinct chemical series which showed strong anti-tumor activity, ultimately enabling us to select SGR-1505 as our development candidate in under two years.
later_quote: By applying advanced physics-based modeling techniques, including combining free energy calculations with machine learning methods and a chemistry-aware compound enumeration workflow, extensive sets of de novo design ideas were explored to quickly identify a novel hit series.
note: 10-K filed 2022-02-24 has the same sentence for the MALT1 program before the code name was public ('enabling development candidate selections in our MALT1 inhibitor program in under two years') and states the development candidate was already selected (no date). Later quote is from the J Med Chem abstract (read via Europe PMC; full text paywalled); 'compound enumeration' is not a generative model, so not coded G3.

design_date_basis: company-stated selection as first development candidate; also first public disclosure under code name
method_quote: The company’s drug discovery platform combines diverse and proprietary chemical libraries of small molecule protein degraders with in-house proteomics, structural biology, AI/machine learning-based target selection and computational chemistry capabilities to predict and obtain protein degradation profiles.
later_quote: Combined with Flash generative designs and GlueAID ADMET models, Rhapsody virtual screens create and identify novel MGDs that are predicted to induce neosubstrate-specific ternary complex formation, have excellent ADMET properties, are available for rapid synthesis, and can be prioritized for follow-up experiments.
note: No candidate-level method source found; 10-K filed 2023-03-16 says only "MRT-2359 was identified using QuEEN TM" (platform, no method). Platform source is the Q3 2021 release (8-K exhibit 99.1) announcing selection of MRT-2359, before trial start 2022-10-12. The S-1 of 2021-06-04 describes Rhapsody as "AI-driven algorithms" that "identify and prioritize MGDs" (also G1). Later attribution is platform-level: the 10-K filed 2024-03-14 names the Flash generative chemistry algorithm; the 10-K filed 2023-03-16 also mentions structures "from predicted protein folding" for target identification.

design_date_basis: first trial start of NCT03715985 (Phase 1/2a), identified as the EVX-01 trial in the F-1 of 2021-01-08
method_quote: EVX-01 immunotherapy consisted of 6 administrations with 5–10 PIONEER TM -predicted neoantigens as synthetic peptides combined with the novel liposome-based Cationic Adjuvant Formulation 09b (CAF®09b) to strengthen T-cell responses.
later_quote: Our proprietary in silico AI modules identifying neoantigens within PIONEER™ have been trained using gradient-boosted decision trees, transformers and a conditional generative adversarial network approach on our internally generated data as well as other data, including, but not limited to, next generation sequencing data from tumor samples, mass spectrometry immunopeptidomics, peptide-MHC-binding affinity data, T-cell immunogenicity data, peptide-MHC-binding stability data.
note: Window uses the brief's trial start 2022-09-19. The F-1 (2021-01-08) shows an earlier EVX-01 Phase 1/2a, NCT03715985, started 2019-01-28 per ClinicalTrials.gov; against that date no source within 12 months was found, and the earliest platform source (F-1 2021-01-08, raw/sources/B_evaxion_F-1_2021-01-08.txt) gives the same coding: "Our proprietary in silico AI models within PIONEER, for the prediction of T-cell activation, allow us to efficiently identify and select those neoepitopes that we believe are most likely to generate a strong, de novo T-cell response leading to significant antitumor effect in each patient." The same paper says PIONEER "allows rank potential neoepitopes". Vintage G1 either way. Later source names a GAN and transformers, but as training methods for modules that identify and rank neoantigens, so coded G1 by what the AI does; a coder reading the G3 list literally (GANs) could code G1;G3.

design_date_basis: company-stated nomination as preclinical candidate ("In February 2021, Insilico Medicine nominated INS018_055 as the preclinical candidate (PCC) for IPF")
method_quote: The molecules were first generated using Insilico's Chemistry42 system, powered by NVIDIA V100 Tensor Core GPUs, that adopts Structure-based Drug Design (SBDD) generative chemistry approach, tested in human cell and animal models.
later_quote: Chemistry42 first applied 30 generative models in parallel to generate compound structures.
note: The 2021-02-24 release announces an unnamed IPF preclinical candidate; its identity with ISM001-055/INS018_055 rests on the 2023-02-08 release (raw/sources/B_insilico_eurekalert_2023-02-08.txt) stating nomination in February 2021. The first source naming the code with a method is a copy of the 2021-12-01 Insilico release on the HKSTP site (raw/sources/B_hkstp_ism001055_2021-12-01.txt): "We have leveraged our end-to-end AI-powered drug discovery platform, including the usage of generative biology and generative chemistry, to discover novel biological targets and generate novel molecules with drug-like properties." (G3). That release reports a microdose trial in Australia first dosed 2021-12-01, earlier than the brief's trial start 2022-02-21. Later paper also names G1 and G4 for target discovery: "PandaOmics was used to prioritize potential candidate targets based on the combination of omic- and text-based models (scores)" and PandaOmics is described as "using multiple AI engines including generative pretrained transformers".

design_date_basis: first public disclosure under code name (release announcing first patient dosed)
method_quote: BenevolentAI creates and applies AI and machine learning to transform the way medicines are discovered and developed.
later_quote: Substantially improved our suite of target identification tools; introduced sophisticated large language models to predict novel therapeutic drug targets from scientific literature
note: Candidate-level text names no method: 'a molecule designed and developed by BenevolentAI'. The platform paragraph says only 'AI and machine learning', without saying what the models do; coded not stated. No dated BenevolentAI filing or prospectus before the trial was found (company was private; investors page refuses scripted access, HTTP 403). The release dates first patient dosing to 11 February 2020, earlier than the brief's 2020-10-14. Later quote is platform-level and describes tools added in 2022, after BEN-2293 entered trials; the same release says BEN-2293 was generated 'Using our platform'. A 2026 Nat Commun paper surfaced by a BEN-2293 search concerns Pfizer's PF-07245303, not BEN-2293.

design_date_basis: first trial start (no earlier disclosure under code name found)
method_quote: The Generate Platform uses machine learning (ML) models to generate therapeutics with desirable properties.
later_quote: Using structure-conditioned machine-learning protein design we optimized two broadly neutralizing sarbecovirus antibodies to rescue the activity of a class 4 anti-RBD antibody against Omicron variants and improve the neutralization profile of an anti-S2 stem antibody, resulting in the identification of the lead candidates PRO-37587 and GB-0669.
note: IDWeek 2023 abstract (presented 2023-10-13, published 2023-11-27), within 12 months of trial start; it states "We used this platform to explore the amino acid sequence landscape" and "The Generate Platform was employed to identify S-2 targeted Spike antibodies with high potency and breadth of neutralization resulting in GB-0669." Later sources describe GB-0669 as optimized from an existing anti-S2 antibody, not designed de novo. ClinicalTrials.gov record was registered retrospectively (first posted 2025-07-03).

design_date_basis: first trial start (earliest disclosure under code name found is the release of 2024-01-04)
method_quote: About Generate:Biomedicines Generate:Biomedicines is the first drug generation company pioneering a machine learning-powered generative biology platform with the ability to create new drugs on demand across a wide range of biologic modalities.
later_quote: Using a generative optimization technology stack, GB-0895 was computationally designed to improve potency and half-life while retaining specificity.
